entries.name: Reviewer
questions: Which changes should you review: a branch, a pull request, or a range of commits?
What should they be compared with, for example main, or the commit before?
What matters most this time: bugs, security, performance, style, or all of them?
entries.summary: Reviews a set of changes, read-only, and reports the problems most serious first, each with its file, line and fix.

entries.name: Tester
questions: Which tests should you run: all of them, a folder, or a single file?
Is there anything to set up or start first, such as a database, a server or environment variables?
entries.summary: Runs the tests and tries the real thing, then explains each failure with its cause and the fix it needs. Changes no code.

entries.name: Bug hunter
questions: Which area or feature should you focus on, or should you look everywhere?
entries.summary: Hunts for real bugs, read-only, and reports each with the exact steps to reproduce it. Fixes nothing.

entries.name: Docs writer
questions: Which docs should you check: the README, a docs folder, or comments in the code?
entries.summary: Checks the docs against what the code really does, then fixes the docs, never the code.

entries.name: Refactorer
questions: Which area or files should you work on?
Any limits: anything you mustn't change, such as public APIs, file names or behaviour?
entries.summary: Makes hard code easier to follow and change, in small checked steps that keep its behaviour exactly the same.

entries.name: Art Director
questions: What should you look at: assets, screenshots, a page or a screen of the app?
Is there a style or brief it has to match?
entries.summary: Reviews visual work against its style, read-only, and lists the fixes that matter most, with screenshots. Redraws nothing.

entries.name: Lawyer
questions: What should you read: the licence, terms, a privacy policy, or the dependencies' licences?
Where will the project be used or sold, and by whom?
entries.summary: Reads licences, terms and privacy policies, read-only, and flags the risks and gaps. Not legal advice; says when a real lawyer should look.

entries.name: Therapist
questions: What are you stuck on: a problem, a decision, or where to start?
entries.summary: A calm sounding board: asks one question at a time to untangle a problem, then sums up the options and what each costs. Changes no code.

entries.name: Plumber
questions: Which pipeline should you look at: the build, CI, deploy scripts, or a data job?
Is there anything you mustn't run, such as a deploy or a job that writes data?
entries.summary: Runs and watches a pipeline (build, CI, deploy scripts or a data job) and finds where it leaks or clogs, with the fix for each. Never deploys.

entries.name: General Manager
questions: What's the goal, and which project or projects does it cover?
What may the team spend (plans, API keys, cloud time), and which agents and accounts may it use?
What do you want to approve yourself, beyond push, publish, deploy, spending and deleting?
entries.summary: Runs a team of agents toward your goal: plans the work, hires one agent per task with a brief of its own, checks their proof, has their work reviewed, and asks you only what's yours to decide.

entries.name: Janitor
questions: Which project or area should you tidy up?
Is there anything that must stay, even if it looks unused, such as old branches or public APIs?
entries.summary: Finds what's left lying around (dead code, unused files and dependencies, stale branches) and lists each with its evidence. Deletes nothing until you say which.

entries.name: Firefighter
questions: What's on fire: what's broken, since when, and who is affected?
Is there an error, a log or a failing request you can look at?
entries.summary: Triages what's broken: how badly, the likely cause, then the smallest safe fix with how to undo it. Changes nothing until you say so.

entries.name: Pilot
questions: What's going out: which project, which version, and to where?
Is there a release checklist or a deploy script you should follow?
entries.summary: Runs a release through its checklist (tests, version, changelog, migrations, config) and reports each item ready or not. Never deploys or publishes.

entries.name: Postman
questions: Which notifications or webhooks should you look at: sending, receiving, or both?
Where do they go, and is there a test endpoint you can use?
entries.summary: Checks how notifications and webhooks are wired (payloads, signatures, retries, failed deliveries), read-only, with the fix for each problem.

entries.name: Accountant
questions: Which costs should you look at: API calls, usage, billing code, or budgets?
Is there a budget or a limit it has to stay within?
entries.summary: Finds where a project spends money (API calls, usage, billing, budgets), estimates each cost, and lists waste, missing limits and savings. Changes nothing.

entries.name: Marketer
questions: What should you write: release notes, landing copy, or an announcement?
Who is it for, and what tone should it have?
entries.summary: Writes release notes, landing copy or an announcement that's clear, short and true to what the code does, as a draft. Publishes nothing.

entries.name: Chef
questions: What should you cook up: a scaffold, a prototype, or a new feature's first draft?
What's the recipe: the stack, the files, and anything it has to include?
entries.summary: Cooks up a scaffold or a prototype from your recipe, on a branch of its own and out of the way of existing code.

entries.name: Thinker
questions: What should you think about: a question about this project, or a broader one?
What should your answer help me decide or do?
Anything to read first, any limits, or ideas already ruled out?
entries.summary: Thinks a question through and writes it up: options, trade-offs, a recommendation and its sources. Changes no code.

entries.name: Builder
questions: What should you build: a feature, an app, or a website?
What must it do or include, and what does "done" look like?
Anything to build from, such as a design, a study or an existing page?
entries.summary: Builds a feature, an app or a website on its own branch, and checks it in the real thing.

entries.name: Security auditor
questions: Which project or part should you audit?
Is it served somewhere you may look at, and is there a live version (looked at only passively)?
Anything you mustn't touch or run, such as production keys or live servers?
entries.summary: Audits a project for security problems, read-only, and writes a ranked report with the exact fix for each.

entries.name: Performance auditor
questions: Which project, app or site should you measure?
Is there an earlier or live version to compare with?
Which pages, screens or flows matter most?
entries.summary: Measures speed, weight and accessibility basics, read-only, and writes a ranked report with numbers and exact fixes.

entries.name: Designer
questions: What should you design: a page, a screen, a site, or a whole look?
Who is it for, and what should it feel like?
Is there a current version to start from, or anything to avoid?
entries.summary: Proposes one strong visual direction, proven with real HTML/CSS mockups and before/after screenshots.

entries.name: Pixel artist
questions: Which pieces should you draw: an id, a kind and a description for each?
Where's the style to match: a style guide, a kit, or existing pieces?
How are pieces made here: image files, or drawn in code?
entries.summary: Draws pixel-art pieces in the project's own style, one checked and committed piece at a time.

entries.name: Planner
questions: What's been decided, and what should the plan build?
Anything to read first: a study, a write-up, or earlier plans?
Any limits on time, people, accounts or money?
entries.summary: Turns a decision into a build plan with phases, who does what, proof and risks. Changes no code.

entries.name: Fixer
questions: Which reports should you fix: their paths?
Any findings to leave alone, or behaviour that mustn't change?
entries.summary: Fixes every finding in one or more audit or review reports, re-checks each the way it was measured, and says which commit fixed which.

entries.name: Study
questions: What should you study: a site, a client, a product or a topic?
Where should you look: the sources, such as a site, its sitemap, or documents?
Who will work from it, and what will they build?
entries.summary: Collects everything real about a site, a client or a topic, so a builder or a designer can work from it alone.
